title: The second derivative

points.text: Linking the graphs of f, f' and f''; concavity

bigPicture: The second derivative measures how the gradient itself changes. It describes the bend (concavity) of a graph and links the graphs of f, f′ and f″.

keyIdeas.cue: Notation and meaning of the second derivative?
keyIdeas.answer: f″(x) or d²y/dx²: the derivative of f′(x), the rate of change of the gradient.

keyIdeas.cue: How are f, f′ and f″ linked, and what is concavity?
keyIdeas.answer: f increasing where f′ > 0; turning points of f where f′ = 0 (and changes sign). f″ > 0: concave up, f′ increasing. f″ < 0: concave down. Turning points of f′ match points of inflexion of f.

workedExamples.title: Concavity
workedExamples.prompt: f(x) = x³ − 3x². Find where f is concave up and the point of inflexion.
steps: f″ > 0 for x > 1; changes sign at x = 1
workedExamples.answer: concave down x < 1, up x > 1; inflexion (1, −2)

misconceptions.right: f″ must change sign (y = x⁴ has f″(0) = 0 but a minimum).

practice.prompt: y = x⁴ − 4x³. Find d²y/dx² and the intervals where the graph is concave up.
f(x) = ln(x² + 1). Use the GDC to sketch y = f″(x) and find the interval on which f is concave up.
solution: GDC: f″(x) > 0 between its zeros x = −1 and x = 1

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: Inflexion needs a sign change of f″
